newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco's sunflower area to expand 25 pct in 96/97.
newsitem.headline: Morocco's sunflower area to expand 25 pct in 96/97.

text.p: Morocco expects its sunflowerseed area to expand by 25 percent to reach 200,000 hectares in 1996/97 season due largely to plenty of rains in winter, the official MAP news agency said on Thursday.
Quoting the association of vegetable oil producers, MAP said the sunflowerseed area was 160,000 hectares in 1995/96 season.
Morocco has had more than double its normal annual rainfall, but has registered a delay in cereals sowings, MAP said.
According to the agriculture ministry, an estimated 65 percent of arable lands have been sown so far. The remainder is expected to be sown mainly to sunflower crops in March.
Heavy rains in December caused delays in ploughing at the normal time, the ministry said.
The association said Morocco's edible oil conglomerate Lesieur has agreed to purchase all domestic sunflowerseed output for 1996/97 season at a floor price of 410 dirhams per quintal (100 kgs).

Morocco produced an estimated 55,000 tonnes of sunflowerseeds and 120,000 tonnes of vegetable oil in 1995/96 season, the association said. This represents an average 20 percent of the country's consumption of edible oil.
It imported nearly 250,000 tonnes of vegetable oil and seeds in 1995 at a cost of 716 million dirhams, the Office des Changes regulatory bureau said. No updated figures were available.

A total of 5.6 million hectares are expected to be sown to all crops in the 1996/97 season, similar to the 1995/96 area, the agriculture ministry said. Nearly 900,000 hectares are in irrigated areas, it added.
